## Reconstructing an event {#event-reconstruction}

::::::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### The idea

<video class="slide-video media-height-lg" style="--media-max-height: 620px;" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" poster="media/reconstruction/reconstruction_en.jpg" src="media/reconstruction/reconstruction_en.mp4"></video>

### Try it

{{< include assets/reconstruction/interactive.html >}}

### The model

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Predict a time for each sensor**

$$
\cos\theta_C=\frac{1}{\beta n_{\rm phase}},\qquad
t_i^{\rm pred}=t_0+\frac{s_i}{\beta c}+\frac{n_{\rm group}D_i}{c}.
$$

$s_i$: muon distance from the known crossing point to emission.

$D_i$: photon path from emission to the sensor.

The cone uses the **phase** index; flight time uses the **group** index.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Find the direction that agrees with the signals**

$$
S=\frac{1}{2\sigma_t^2}\sum_{i,k}
\left(t_{ik}^{\rm obs}-t_i^{\rm pred}\right)^2
\longrightarrow\min_{\theta,\phi,t_0}.
$$

Every detected photoelectron contributes a measured time.

**Here:** known crossing point, straight muon, homogeneous medium.
Only direction and time offset are fitted — not vertex or energy.
:::
:::::

::: {.question}
How does a wrong model of the medium change the inferred direction?
:::

::: {.small}
Synthetic teaching model, not an experiment's reconstruction or an angular-resolution forecast.
The arrow is the muon's direction of travel; the source direction is opposite.
:::
::::::
:::::::
